agree.reason: A long-serving teller who doesn't want phone work gets sympathy but no concrete reasons to stay: the $1.50 raise, first pick of shifts by seniority and the option to try the role and still take severance within 6 months are all missing, so many would start looking elsewhere.

honest.reason: It drops the unsupported 'better for everyone' and avoids overclaiming, but it says the center is open 'three more hours a day' when 8 to 8 against 9 to 5 is four, and it states as fact that the change will cut wait times without support.

works_the_facts.reason: The 44% and 60% figures are restated but nothing is worked out from them, the hours difference is miscalculated, and 'same pay or higher' is used where the actual $1.50-an-hour raise was available, along with no worked severance example.

right_comparison.reason: Falling visits and the 9-minute hold time suggest what the status quo looks like, but the email never says what would happen if the branches stayed open, and it never gives staff a clear side-by-side of the new role against severance.

qualification.reason: Staff need dates to act on, and the email gives none: no written offers by February 14, no March 1 decision deadline and no HR one-on-one, only 'reply to this email'.

objections.reason: It names the worry about rotating shifts and childcare but answers it only with work-from-home days, says nothing to staff who dislike phone work, and opens with 'hear this from me first' to people who heard the rumours two weeks ago.

fit.reason: It is an email of roughly 400 words with a subject line and clear sections, but it has no sign-off from the COO even though it was meant to come from her.
